title.narrative: Sustainable Rural Infrastructure and Watershed Management Sector Project - Additional Financing

description.narrative: On 20 September 2019, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) approved the Sustainable Rural Infrastructure and Watershed Management Sector Project (SRIWMSP) for $51.5 million financed by an ADB concessional loan of $40.0 million, an ADB grant (ADF) of $5.0 million, a European Union (EU) grant of $4.5 million equivalent, and government contribution of US$2.0 million equivalent. The ADB loan and ADB grant closing date is 31 December 2028, while the EU grant is 30 September 2027. The project aims at improving rural incomes from market-driven diversified farm output, watershed health, and community nutrition in the four northern provinces of Houaphan, Louangphabang, Xaignabouli, and Xiangkhouang by (i) promoting diversification into dry season high-value crops (HVCs) and improving the yields of wet season rice by providing irrigation and access; (ii) protecting watershed ecological services; and (iii) improving nutrition. The project also benefits from parallel co-financing from IFAD of about US$21.0 million and from GIZ of about EUR20 million.

Output: Indicator Indicator: 18 PLUPs implemented. Progress/Status: Loan Implementation Consultants for the Department of Irrigation, Houaphan, Xiengkhouang, and Luang Prabang/Xayaboury were recruited and mobilized.
ADB approved the revised guidelines for preparation of the Participatory Land Use Plans (PLUPs) in April 2023 and procurement of field equipment for the technical field teams in May 2023. Implementation of the plans for Xiengkhouang and Houaphan provinces are ongoing. The Mission reminded PGT that safeguards would be a key issue to be considered in the preparation and implementation of the PLUPs and the project's resettlement framework would need to be followed. Data Source: PPMS Actual value:

Output: Indicator Indicator: 18 subprojects modernized Progress/Status: Civil works for 4 RSPs are on track. Construction for Xieng Khouang for Nam Tong is completed and handed over in May 2023. The Nam Poua bridge construction in Houaphan is completed and is for final inspection. The Nam Poua project is 88% completed. The Nam Phieng is 90% complete and Luang Prabang Nam Seng project is 80% complete in Xayabouly.
Preparation of the first batch of Batch 2 is ongoing including 9 subprojects. Surveys and detailed designs including hydrological and social and environmental safeguards assessments were completed in 2022. However, during the review mission of November 2022, ADB requested PGT to prepare feasibility studies for the eight ASPs. A first round of ASPs were shared with ADB in Q2 2023 in which ADB requested their revision. The revised feasibility studies still need revisions, mainly with two aspects: (i) upgrading of irrigation infrastructure should be based on future climate scenarios rather than historic data-sets, (ii) the feasibility studies should demonstrate how diversion to high-value crops will be achieved. The mission highlighted the importance of the feasibility studies, which demonstrate the subproject's ability to meet the selection criteria and project objectives as laid out in the PAM, especially those relating to climate resilience, economic justification and financial sustainability. Feasibility studies are expected to be completed by mid-Q2, 2024, followed by the tendering process during the wet season. Ideally the civil works of the second batch of ASPs shall start in Nov 2024 during the dry season. The Mission recommends the EA to expedite the process of preparing the feasibility studies as it appears to take approximately four months after completion of the detailed engineering designs.
Preparations for Batch 3 subprojects are ongoing with data collection for topographical, geotechnical, and hydrological surveys, preparation of draft FSRs, pre-designs and final draft OED, and preparation of draft IEEs and social guard assessments. Data Source: PPMS Actual value:

Output: Indicator Indicator: Plans implemented for water control systems involving 120 WUGs with WUGs members comprising both husband and wife names. (2018 baseline: 2 WUGs) (OP 2.1, OP 5.3) Progress/Status: Strengthening of the water user groups (WUGs) is underway, which involves some restructuring and capacity building. Following discussions with local stakeholders and producers, it is proposed that the WUGs will also have a second function, i.e. market connectivity. This will be monitored in future missions. DOI also reported that a dialogue has now been opened with the WUGs on the application of irrigation service fees. The existing WUGs in the target areas are in different stages of formation and development. The current status is as follows: (i) Houaphan - Nam Pua RSP has existing WUGs, but with limited roles; (ii) Luang Prabang - Nam Seng RSP has existing WUGs, but with limited roles; (iii) Xayaboury - Nam Phieng RSP has well established WUGs that collect fees and operate bank accounts; and (iv) Xieng Khouang - WUGs have been established at Nam Tong (RSP), Nam Kha, Nam Pew, Nam Mud and Nam Guer.
